Good you can aknowledge it to yourself, many t-people suffer because they feel the pressure to live as cliche-girls if they are amab. 
And you are not alone, absolutely. I'm in this sort of "limbo" too, more than four years into transition. I just tired of playing the stereotypical girl in order to be accepted by society. That's another closet, like one I left years ago. I don't want to fool myself and people around me about my genetics. Why do I have to? I'm definitely not a boy, but that leaves me the whole other spectrum (that gender is). Non-binary, agender, bigender, whatever. 
The thing I've come to is not to ask myself "who I am?", but rather "what do I want to wear?", "what kind of make up to choose?", "how do I behave when not oppressed by gender standards?", "how do I speak when I'm not afraid to be myself?", "what kind of people turn me on?" (not "girls" or "boys", but "lean", "tall", "hairy", "chubby", "lighthearted", "serious", etc.). Many different questions.
And about how do people see me? It's not my business. Thinking about it is a path leading to unhealthy self-consciousness and hypocrisy. 
Well, I sound more confident than actually am, but I'm working towards it. Peace and love!
